clue.text: Girl straddles a horse belonging to James

indicators.note: to straddle is to sit with legs either side, so the girl's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A girl sits astride a horse owned by a man named James.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belonging to James' looks like a phrase about a person, but Jacobus is Latin for James, which gives the adjective for his era.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes things from the reign of King James I, so it is an adjective of possession tied to that king.

clue.text: Bully for him!

parts.note: the exclamation of mock praise is reread as a man's name that also means to bully

explanation.walkthrough: To hector is to bully, and Hector is also a man's name, so the name is one that suits a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb hector means to browbeat or intimidate, and it is also a boy's name, the Trojan hero.

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction with a break in service

definitions.text: Express dissatisfaction with a break in service

parts.words: Express dissatisfaction with a break in service
parts.note: looks like a grumble about a tennis service break, but simply describes grumbling when a supply fails

explanation.walkthrough: A 'break in service' suggests tennis, but it is just an interruption to a utility, something people grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble or protest is a plain synonym for voicing dissatisfaction.

clue.text: It checks the growth of population

definitions.text: It checks the growth of population

parts.words: It checks the growth of population
parts.note: 'checks' suggests restraining growth, as birth control would, but here means counts and monitors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' seems to mean curbs, like a policy limiting births, but an official headcount only checks in the sense of measuring.
explanation.definitionFit: An official periodic count of a country's people measures how its population has grown.

clue.text: Stopped wearing corsets

definitions.meaning: stopped in the sense of remained or did not leave
stays are old-fashioned corsets, so someone in them is laced up in stays

explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means remained, and stays were boned corsets, so a stayed figure is one wearing them.

clue.text: Achieved one's goal?

parts.note: an ambition achieved is reread literally as a ball put into a goal

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as reaching an aim; the question mark hints at the football sense of putting the ball in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Scored means got a goal or point in a game, which is literally achieving a goal.

clue.text: Knock out a large quantity of foreign money

parts.note: KO is the standard abbreviation for a boxing knockout
a peck, as in 'a peck of trouble', is a large amount

explanation.surface: A boxer flattens an opponent and wins a heap of foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck is a Russian coin worth a hundredth of a rouble, so it is foreign currency.

clue.text: Light linked to switch

indicators.note: to switch things is to swap them around, so the letters of the neighbouring word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lamp is wired up to a switch on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like part of the electrical picture but is the anagram signal on 'linked'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to set it burning, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Sad mourners hit the gin

indicators.note: a sad state of affairs is a poor arrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Grief-stricken people at a wake turn to the gin bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' reads as the mood of the mourners but signals rearranging MOURNERS HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother's ruin is an old British slang name for gin, from its ruinous effect in the 18th century.

clue.text: Policeman not allowed to evade responsibility

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
out means ruled out or not permitted

explanation.surface: An officer is barred from dodging his duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is an idiom for avoiding a commitment or duty one ought to face.

clue.text: Not in favour of work — puzzling!

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
posing, as in posing a problem, means puzzling or baffling

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a task decides they are against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is a direct synonym for not supporting it.

clue.text: Only I object to scripture lessons

parts.note: the pronoun I in its object form is me
RE is religious education, the school subject once called scripture

explanation.surface: A pupil protests at having to sit through Bible classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest but means the object case of 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child, so it matches only or just.

clue.text: Opportunities to check the lines after casting

definitions.text: Opportunities to check the lines after casting

parts.words: Opportunities to check the lines after casting
parts.note: casting and lines suggest an angler's tackle, but it is actors going through their script

explanation.walkthrough: Lines after casting sounds like fishing, but once a play is cast the actors practise their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice sessions for a play let the cast run through their script before opening night.

clue.text: Untimely error possibly made by a Cornishman

indicators.note: 'possibly made by' says these letters could be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: A man from Cornwall might be to blame for a mistake in timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of A CORNISHMAN; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in the wrong period, like a clock in ancient Rome, is a chronological mistake.

clue.text: The actors have to press hard

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a production
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron, the brittle metal, describes anything firm or unbreakable, as in a cast-iron alibi.

clue.text: Cushy job at home in safe environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds what lives in it, so the word for safe goes round the other piece

parts.note: secure means safe
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: An easy post you can do from home in comfortable surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work, an easy berth.

clue.text: Rock one sailor climbed with another

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing goes upwards, so the first sailor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a salt, an old seaman, is another sailor

explanation.surface: One seaman scaled a rock face alongside a shipmate.
explanation.walkthrough: AB reversed gives BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, an example of rock.

clue.text: A kiss, say, indicates attachment

indicators.note: say signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a kiss is written X, so 'a kiss' gives an X, pronounced 'an ex'

explanation.surface: A peck on the cheek shows that someone is fond of you.
explanation.walkthrough: X for a kiss is read as a letter name, and 'an ex' spoken matches the answer; 'indicates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, so it is an attachment.

clue.text: Shop Irishman is opening, with Ireland's backing

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for Ireland's is turned round

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: An Irish man launches a shop with his country's financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: EIRES reversed gives SERIE; 'opening, with' is a link to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a cake shop, a specific kind of shop.

clue.text: He suffered from soaring ambition

parts.note: 'soaring ambition' sounds figurative but is literal flight too near the sun

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this boy flew too close to the sun on wax wings, which melted.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of Greek myth fell to his death after flying too high on his father's wings.

clue.text: Altogether Ben fails to set up pass

indicators.note: the name fails to stay intact, so its letters are reordered
in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the word for pass reverses

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Ben can't get through a mountain crossing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN rearranged gives ENB; COL reversed gives LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French borrowed into English for as a whole, all together.

clue.text: Women in retreat

parts.note: retreat suggests fleeing an army, but means a religious withdrawal from the world

explanation.walkthrough: A retreat is also a religious house or a time of seclusion, where these women live.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a female religious order live withdrawn from the world, as in a convent.

clue.text: Ceremonial departure

parts.note: departure here means departing this life, a ritual death

explanation.walkthrough: Departure is a euphemism for death; the Japanese ritual suicide was a formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hara-kiri is the Japanese ritual suicide by disembowelment, a formal way to die.

clue.text: It may go down well, but one dies to kick it

definitions.text: It may go down well, but one dies to kick it

parts.words: It may go down well, but one dies to kick it
parts.note: 'go down well' means descend a well

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down well' seems to mean be welcomed, but is a pail lowered into a well; to kick the bucket is to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is lowered into a well for water, and kicking it is an idiom for dying.

clue.text: German, sadly far from fortunate, is in trouble

indicators.note: sadly signals a sorry state, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German, far from lucky, finds himself in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far from fortunate' removes F, A, R from FORTUNATE, and 'sadly' rearranges the remaining OTUNTE; 'is in trouble' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Teuton is an old or jocular word for a German, from an ancient Germanic tribe.

clue.text: Score confused with a gross

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tally gets muddled with a dozen dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 144, partnering 'Score' as 20, but means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and gross are synonyms for crude or vulgar.
